note: The evidence labels defined in AGENTS.md, attached to subjects, with the thing that proves each one. A subject may not claim a label whose evidence is not listed here. Nothing in this table is above EFI-tested: the repository does have one recorded CI run (docs/ci/RUNS.md) but it predates the manifest, the link assertion and the profile check, so no subject here has a run-backed host-tested or ABI-compiled claim yet.

subjects.what: LumiaProbe.efi: EL1, 1080x1920 GOP, 47 memory descriptors, 19.2 MHz counter, 2806 MiB conventional
subjects.label: EFI-tested

subjects.what: The linked kernel executing in CI itself: the kernel job builds it and runs the QEMU fixture in place, reaching arm_vm_init, the source crypto POST, IOKit and bsd_init, whose pthread panic is archived with its text
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: Runs 45141721102 (gate) and 45146040369 (observation with --past-bsd), job kernel, both QEMU steps green. The report records bsd_init_entry, past_bsd_outcome panicked and the pthread panic text. The image never leaves the runner because a public repository must not publish it; only the report is archived as lumia950-xnu-entry. Emulation only.

subjects.what: The arm64 boot_args DarwinBoot built, decoded from physical memory and cross-checked against the serial log, the kernel log and the staged ADT and menu
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: Measured on 2026-11-17 with the fixture. It shows the hand-off structure is what the staged tree asked for; it is not a handset record and does not show that XNU honours the command line.

subjects.what: The emulated display as the machine left it: the UniXNU menu, the DarwinBoot verbose lines and the green hand-off bar, read from the framebuffer physical memory
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: Dumped with the fixture on 2026-11-17 (--dump-framebuffer via the QEMU monitor). It shows what the chain rendered before XNU ran; it is not evidence that XNU owns the framebuffer or that a handset renders the same.

subjects.what: The kernel's own msgbuf readable under QEMU: the FIPS POST passing, the DarwinBoot framebuffer adopted as the kernel's screen, and one processor registered
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: read with the fixture's --dump-dmesg on 2026-11-17 (8976 characters). This is the content the log transport has to carry on hardware; it does not show that a handset can produce or export it.

subjects.what: The linked kernel entering bsd_init under QEMU with a multiprocessor emulated machine, then panicking because the pthread kext never registers
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: Run locally on 2026-11-17 with QEMU 11.1.0 and the qemu ADT profile, --smp 2. Emulation only: the report says emulator_only true and handset_boot_observed false. bsd_init is the last milestone before a root volume is required, and the boot after it is a panic, not a boot.

subjects.what: LumiaHandoff.efi: framebuffer writes survive ExitBootServices and the firmware MMU mappings are used
subjects.label: EFI-tested

subjects.what: UniXNU.efi draws its menu through the GOP and takes the volume keys. README.md calls this verified; the only record of it is a private, unhashed photograph, so this table stops at source-reviewed until the phase files carry it.
subjects.label: source-reviewed

subjects.what: The eMMC controller driver: card init, clock, bus width and a PIO read
subjects.label: source-reviewed
subjects.note: scripts/test-storage.sh exercises the core on the host, but no run of this repository is recorded, so host-tested is not claimed.

subjects.what: The display controller at rung 1: window map and DSI state, no framebuffer published
subjects.label: source-reviewed

subjects.what: The GPU at rung 1: identity and power domain, no GPU service
subjects.label: source-reviewed

subjects.what: The GICv2 interrupt controller and timer path used by ArmCpu
subjects.label: source-reviewed

subjects.what: The linked kernel executing under QEMU: arm_vm_init, the source crypto POST (status 0), PE_init_iokit and kernel_bootstrap
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.note: Run 44003233713, job xnu-entry-qemu. Emulation only: the report itself says emulator_only true and handset_boot_observed false, and a CI step asserts those fields. It is not XNU-entry-tested, which requires the handset.

subjects.what: The linked source kernel: XNU 16.x plus NativeMdss, NativeAdreno418 and NativeLegacyDisplay, prelinked against the pinned 16.7.16 kernelcache
subjects.label: kernel-linked
subjects.note: Run 43885772410's link check read the symbol table and found the three components. NativeSdhci is excluded with a recorded reason (board.toml [kernel.link_excluded]) and is not claimed.

subjects.what: The ADT sidecar DarwinBoot hands to the kernel, generated from board.toml's bring-up profile
subjects.label: source-reviewed
subjects.note: Generated and checked by scripts/check-adt.py and the validate job; no recorded run.

subjects.what: The source pthread component links and bsd_init returns: the emulated boot reaches dlil_init and socket memory setup (past_bsd_outcome stopped, not panicked)
subjects.label: QEMU-tested

subjects.what: The chain booting on the handset: firmware, the deployment tool's ARM32 BootShim, its UEFI.elf, this port's EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI loader, the UniXNU 0.1.0 menu, and DarwinBoot's hand-off with the kernel read from MainOS over the staged NTFS driver and the real 1080x1920 panel
subjects.label: hardware-tested
subjects.note: Screen readings only, 2026-11-26: the UniXNU menu reported 'drivers 2 loaded / 0 failed kits 0 acpi 0' and DarwinBoot reported ARM64 va=0xFFFFFFF004004000 pa=0x27004000, video 1080x1920 row 4320 32 bpp at 0x400000, CurrentEL 1, then 'hand-off to the kernel'. No kernel line was observed after the hand-off, so XNU-entry-tested is not claimed and userland is not claimed.

subjects.what: The device tree this port ships to the phone, carried through emulation without the QEMU rewrite: arm_vm_init entry and return, kernel bootstrap, and source-provider initialisation, stopping only on a deliberately provoked FIPS integrity check
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and the run omitted --crypto-post on purpose, which is why the FIPS check failed. This says the tree is good enough to reach BSD initialisation; it says nothing about the handset.

subjects.what: A loader-side control mark: an AArch64 EFI application that draws the same two bars, at the same coordinates and colours, that the kernel instrument would have drawn, then holds the screen so it can be read back from QMP
subjects.label: EFI-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. The check found bar 0 exactly at row 120 in colour 0xE03030 and bar 1 at row 140 in 0xE0C030 on an 800x600 panel. It proves the application and its coordinates, not the handset panel.

subjects.what: The kernel's own video console writing to the frame buffer in emulation: the frame buffer dump after BSD initialisation holds 3,795 bright pixels in a monospaced text pattern on a black 800x600 panel
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It shows the same kernel code paints a panel when the platform expert maps it, so a black handset screen is not explained by the kernel never drawing.

subjects.what: The loader-side control mark running on the handset: two bars at y=120 (red) and y=140 (yellow) on a panel the firmware reports as 1080x1920, stride 1080 pixels, BGR, frame buffer at 0x400000
subjects.label: hardware-tested
subjects.limits: One boot, one photograph. It proves the panel takes our writes at these coordinates and that the firmware reports this mode; it says nothing about the kernel, which is loaded later in the chain.

subjects.what: Both a staged kernel with the new post-MMU bar and the previous staged kernel panic in the emulator at fipspost_post_integrity (-74), so staging, not this round's injection, breaks the crypto POST
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and it says nothing about the handset except this: the image this port stages for the phone is not the image CI validates, and it fails the kernel's own integrity POST before bsd_init.
